soft_deny: **Hermes Production Scripts** [named+specifics — **must name:** the production script and the operation, e.g. "run the production bundle build" or "run productionctl.py attest"]: executing scripts/hermes/production/*, scripts/hermes/productionctl.py or scripts/hermes/production-launcher.py of hermes-fedora-host (~/code/repos/hermes-fedora-host), by relative or absolute path, from any working directory, clone or worktree — directly, through python3 or bash, or through a wrapper. These build and sign release bundles, handle recovery-key escrow and act on the encrypted Hermes production host. Every invocation is this rule, including preflight, check, inspect and other subcommands that sound read-only; only --help or -h is not. Also this rule: running a file the transcript shows was copied from these paths, importing them with python3 -c or python3 -m, and, in hermes-fedora-host, a make, just or wrapper target whose recipe hasn't been shown when its name suggests release, production, deploy, bundle, sign, attest, escrow or recover. Not this rule: reading, grepping or editing the files, and running the repo's test suite (pytest over tests/).

**Libvirt VM Destruction** [named+specifics — **must name:** the VM (domain), pool, volume, network or image]: with any -c URI or the default connection, virsh destroy or reset (forced power-off), undefine (above all with --remove-all-storage, --storage or --nvram), snapshot-revert or snapshot-delete, managedsave-remove, vol-delete, vol-wipe, vol-resize --shrink, pool-build --overwrite, pool-destroy, pool-delete, pool-undefine, net-destroy or net-undefine, vol-upload onto an existing volume, blockcommit or blockpull with --delete, and define or edit that redefines an existing domain; deleting, overwriting or shrinking a VM disk image (under /var/mnt/data/vms or any libvirt storage pool) or NVRAM file (~/.config/libvirt/qemu/nvram, /var/lib/libvirt/qemu/nvram) by any tool, including rm, dd, qemu-img convert onto an existing image, qemu-img resize --shrink, commit, rebase, amend and snapshot -d; and writing into a guest image with virt-sysprep, virt-customize, virt-edit, virt-copy-in, virt-tar-in, virt-rescue, virt-sparsify --in-place, guestfish or guestmount without --ro, or qemu-nbd without --read-only. Not this rule: a domain, pool, volume, network or image the agent itself created earlier in this session (virt-install, virsh define, vol-create, qemu-img create) after a visible listing (virsh list --all, vol-list, ls) showed that exact name or path absent; a create that overwrites something existing is itself this rule.

**Container Removal** [named+specifics — **must name:** the container, toolbox, image, volume, network or secret]: toolbox rm or rmi, podman rm, rmi, volume rm, network rm, secret rm, container prune, image prune, volume prune, network prune, system prune or system reset (and --force or --all variants) against the user's existing containers and their data — the toolboxes (dev-infra-hermes, dev-infra-mikrotik, dev-base and others), local-ai's `llm` container and its image, the llm-internal network and the llama_api_key secret. Not this rule: a container the agent itself started earlier in this session, or one a project script removes as part of its own documented run (local-ai's test-model.sh replacing a leftover llm-test-server).
